body:
> **Status:** Proposal; target LayerFS v0.1.7; not a released contract.

Release: [#155](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/155).
Implementation parent: [#165](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/165).
Core review: [#172](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/172) (Stage 7) reviews C1/C2 architecture flexibility and pluggability before subsequent integration design.
Sibling pairs: [#179](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/179) (projection & runtime) · [#181](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/181) (boundary & trust).

## Sequencing — owner direction, 2026-09-20

Stage 7 is a review of cluster 1 (content) + cluster 2 (storage), replacing its former runtime implementation scope. This co-design pair and its siblings own the subsequent integration design; implementation and integrated qualification are scoped after those designs. #171 remains the closed core qualification, not acceptance of a future runtime.

The integration must consume reviewed public contracts so that compatible C1/C2 algorithm revisions can be developed independently and substituted without rewriting integration logic. Record any required contract change explicitly; do not make integration depend on private content/storage algorithms, SQL or pack layouts. #172's parallel-worktree substitution scenario is the review's proof obligation, not an instruction to implement this pair during that review.

## Why this is a co-design pair

The operational half already exists as a document; the semantic half does not.

```text
   01-init-commit-and-concurrency   ◄── co-designed ──►   C5 HISTORY
   ──────────────────────────────                         ──────────
   describes the OPERATIONS                               defines the SEMANTICS
    ① prepare → ② commit point                             what a commit IS
    → ③ publish → ④ stage → ⑤ merge                       the parent chain
                                                           what a layer IS
                                                           discard
                                                           scope_allocator
```

**The stage/merge boundary IS the history interface.** The document already
specifies the CAS precisely; what it cannot specify is what the thing being CASed
*means*. Change the meaning of a stage — durable or advisory, deletable or not —
and the stage step changes. Neither contract is complete alone.

**Empirically supported:** the reference keeps both in **one crate**,
`layerfs-layerstack-store` (18,376 production lines — its largest), holding the
CAS/packs/SQLite *and* `commits` / `branches` / `layers` / `layer_stacks` /
`workspace_stages`. History was never operationally separable from the store. Core
has C2 without it, which is exactly why the commit document has a hole at ④/⑤.

## What it produces

- the commit and layer identity model, and what `parent` implies
- the stage: durable or advisory, and what `discard` does
- inode serial allocation (`scope_allocator`) — **C1 refuses to own this**
- the schema: core has **four** tables; the reference has **eight** plus the allocator

## Already settled by discussion

| Decision | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| **Objects immutable, packs append-only** | there is **no `UPDATE objects`**; the only two UPDATEs in the storage layer are the pack append and the watermark |
| **The merge is O(1)** | 1 SELECT · 1 INSERT whose `root_id` IS the commit's `root_id` reused verbatim · 1 CAS. Zero objects created, read or copied |
| **A stale merge is refused, not queued** | applying a commit built against `L0` after the head moved to `L1` promotes a tree lacking `L1`'s changes — a queue that applies in arrival order silently **reverts** |
| **The queue belongs in the runtime** | its unit of work is *rebase then merge*, and rebasing needs the caller's edit stream, which the store does not hold |
| **Commits to different branches never contend** | every branch-level structure is a different row; the CAS target is per-branch |
| **Divergent edits cannot conflict** | different bytes → different ids → different rows. Confirmed by the absence of any in-place modification |

## Open — this is history's half

- [ ] **Commit identity and the parent chain.** Is a branch's chain linear? Is a
      commit immutable once written? What does `parent_commit_id` guarantee?
- [ ] **Commit versus layer.** Why both exist, how a layer relates to a commit, and
      what the layer-stack ordering promises.
- [ ] **Is a stage durable?** A `workspace_stages` row is an ordinary row today.
      Whether it survives a restart, and whether a discarded workspace deletes it,
      changes the commit step.
- [ ] **Discard semantics.** Delete the row only, or account for the objects the
      workspace produced? There is **no GC**, so "discard" currently means
      "unreferenced bytes accumulate".
- [ ] **`scope_allocator`.** Inode serials are allocated by the caller and C1 only
      validates range. Who allocates, is an allocation durable, does an exposed
      serial survive a discarded workspace, and what makes serials unique across a
      store holding many projects? **Zero-copy fork depends on this.**
- [ ] **The schema.** Core's four tables do not carry `commits`, `branches`,
      `layers`, `layer_stacks`, `workspace_stages` or `scope_allocator`. Any of
      these is a schema version bump.
- [ ] **Whether this is a port or a redesign.** If the reference's model is being
      carried over, this pair collapses to reading its tables and documenting the
      semantics — a much smaller job, and the document becomes descriptive rather
      than a proposal.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The document set states, for each of the four phases ①–⑤, what is durable
      and what is advisory.
- [ ] Commit, layer and stage identities are defined with their immutability and
      ordering guarantees.
- [ ] `discard` is defined in terms of rows **and** objects, with the
      no-GC consequence stated rather than implied.
- [ ] Inode serial allocation has an owner, a uniqueness scope and a stated
      behaviour when a workspace is discarded.
- [ ] Every new table is a declared schema version with the open/validate
      consequences stated, in the style of the existing `user_version` history.
- [ ] The races-versus-conflicts boundary is restated: this pair defines
      *detection* only, and divergence detection stays with
      [#164](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/164) (v0.2.0).
- [ ] No worker count, timeout or cache policy is raised to make a case pass.

## Boundary

- **No diff or conflict resolution.** Deferred to
  [#164](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/164) by owner decision
  (2026-09-16). Until it lands, a rebase resolves overlapping edits **silently** —
  a known semantic gap to document, not a bug to fix here.
- **No GC.** Reclamation is out of scope; this pair states the accumulation, it
  does not solve it.
- **`init_namespace` keeps its multi-worker exception** and its 2.7 s cold Init
  target. It creates history rather than staging into it, and it must not be
  collapsed into the commit path.
- **Concurrency prerequisites are separate.** Insert-or-reuse, private packs and
  per-save publication are required before more than one writer exists; they are
  registered under [#177](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/177)
  and [#178](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/178), not here.

## Non-goals

- The projection and the accumulator — [#179](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/179).
- Transport, authorization, tenancy — [#181](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/181).
- Measured integration acceptance — define it with the subsequent implementation; #171 remains evidence for its core-only scope.
title: v0.1.7 co-design pair 2: commit and history — the stage/merge boundary and the timeline it feeds
